### Step 6 — Review

The moment of a check is set by its cost model: machine checks run early and often, mind checks run once, on the settled whole. Review is therefore one sitting at Step 6, after the last build row has landed and the regression and the walk are on disk: a reading by a mind costs minutes whatever it finds, and cannot see across pieces until the head is settled.

**The readers.** The rigor deals the three questions `evidence` · `adversarial` · `structure`: at `single` the critic holds `evidence`, `adversarial` and `structure`; at `double` the auditor holds `evidence` and the critic the other two. There is no third reader: `structure` is a question the critic holds, and its `reuse` and `one-site` findings are rated on the debt table. The auditor falsifies the *evidence* and never reviews the code; the critic falsifies the *code*. A reader is never the author nor a fork of the orchestrator, and is shown no other reader's verdict. Its brief names its questions on a line of its own, `Questions: <q>[, <q>]`, exactly the set the plan's rigor deals its role, or the dispatch wall refuses it; and nothing of their checks: `payload/context/checks-<question>.md` is delivered to it at start, and a paraphrase is a weaker second source. It writes one record per question it is dealt, and its brief lists every record on `Files:`, `Expected artifact:` naming one of them. The reader dealt `evidence`, whichever role holds it, declares one to three runs in all, suites under `Suites:` and other runners under `Re-executes:`; `Suites: none` with no `Re-executes:` is for a reader not dealt `evidence`.

**The reading, once.** The readers are dispatched once, when the last build row has landed, in the one batch `steps/5.md` dispatches. Each reads the settled whole (`scope: whole`), the pieces together and never each piece again, and `proof-add review` registers the reading. Its findings go to the sitting, never to a task list.

**The record and its fact.** Each record is a file under `record/` with flush-left lines `reviewed: <a>..<b>`, `question: <q>`, `result: <pass|flag|fail>`, `scope: <piece|whole>`; for `structure`, one line `check: <id> <PASS|FLAG|FAIL|n/a> <reason>` per check id. When the reader's roster row carries `severity` in `pushed=`, the record also holds `findings: <n>`, one `finding: <n> <S1|S2|S3|S4> <on|off> <path>:<line>|- <title>` per finding, `shown: <n> <command>` for each finding the table sends to fix and `unsure: <n> <what is not known>` for a finding that owes a check (`payload/context/severity.md`); it writes no priority, and one that does is refused when it differs from the table. Otherwise a record with no `findings:` line registers with `result:` as written. Register it with `session-poker.sh proof-add review <record> --question <q> --reader <name>`, `<record>` spelled `record/…` from the docs root or as an absolute path: the head is the record's `b`; the reader's role is read from its roster row, never typed. Code past a question's last head is uncovered for that question.

**A finding the reader cannot settle owes a check, and a move is the user's word.** An `unsure:` line makes its finding a check owed, a `check:` line on the plan. A check record under `record/`, naming its `written-by:` agent (neither the finding's reader nor the code's writer), settles it with `session-poker.sh finding-check <record>#<n> settled <S> <reach> | refuted | unsettled <check record>`, and `current 8` waits on every open one. `session-poker.sh finding-move <record>#<n> <defer|fix> '<the user's words>' '<why>'` moves a finding across the line, on the main thread only, and only on words the user typed in a prompt of this session: at least three whole words, or their whole prompt. A pasted block, a tool result and another agent's text are not theirs, and an S1 is never deferred. A record path registers one pass; the `check:`, `deferred:` and `moved:` lines that bind a finding belong to that pass, so a later pass is written to a new record path.

**The sitting.** A finding is a triage item, never a task. The orchestrator brings every finding to the user with its severity and a recommendation: fix now, Known limit or next wave. The user rules the set. A row exists only from that ruling, recorded on the row with the user's attribution. The one row the orchestrator may make alone is an in-diff finding inside `fix-policy:` and under `fix-cap:`, marked `born: review S<n> <reach>`, and the sitting says so. A debt finding is not brought for a ruling: its disposition is burn-when-touched, and the orchestrator records it at the sitting with `session-poker.sh debt add <record>` (`## Debt ledger` in `operational-rules.md`). Only readers rate: a finding's severity and reach are written by the reader that found it, and no agent, the orchestrator included, moves a rating in either direction; a user's re-rating is recorded with attribution.

**Three stop rules.** In-diff only: a finding in code the run did not change is a next-wave item unless it is S1. Three fixes on one component stop the run. A fix row is never re-read by a fresh pass.

**The waiver is the user's.** `session-poker.sh waive <question> '<reply>'` writes `waived: question=<q> head=<40-hex> by <git user.name> <ISO-UTC> "<reason>"`, covering that question up to that head. An agent never waives.
